          "text": "# The Iris Nebula: A blue bloom in Cepheus\n\n*NGC 7023 is a meeting of young starlight and cosmic dust\u2014and a rewarding challenge for observers under a dark northern sky.*\n\nOn a clear autumn evening, turn your telescope toward Cepheus, the constellation shaped like a house standing high in the north. SIMBAD lists NGC 7023 as an open cluster, while the familiar \u201cIris Nebula\u201d is its luminous reflection nebula. In a reflection nebula, dust scatters light from nearby stars rather than shining through the same process as the glowing gas in many emission nebulae. The dust gives the Iris its characteristic blue cast in photographs. Its central illuminating star, HD 200775, is young; the surrounding material belongs to a region where stars and their natal clouds meet.\n\nThat meeting is visible in images as both brilliance and absence: blue light scattered around the star, and dark dust silhouetted against the glow. In autumn, when Cepheus is high during evening hours, the target is especially convenient.
